| [docs/07-example-repos.md](docs/07-example-repos.md)     | Annotated breakdown of two real-world repositories           |
| [docs/08-pitfalls.md](docs/08-pitfalls.md)               | Common mistakes and a pre-flight checklist                   |
| [docs/stubs/](docs/stubs/)                               | TODO stubs for intentionally excluded topics                 |

## Sources and reliability of this guide

This guide was compiled from:

1. Official VoxelCore documentation (`doc/ru/` — richer, and `doc/en/` — smaller).
   Both are incomplete and contain errors; where they disagreed with reality,
   real pack files were preferred.
2. The engine's own stock pack `res/content/base/` (ground truth for file formats).
3. A working game project:
   [wooden_meat_game](https://github.com/George-Noise/wooden_meat_game)
   (unfinished, but runs).
4. A real UI-focused pack:
   [fork_of_kompot](https://github.com/George-Noise/fork_of_kompot)
   (fork of the Kompot declarative-UI pack; unfinished).

The guide targets the current `main` branch of VoxelCore (engine ~0.32 era,
October 2026 snapshot). It is **not version-pinned**: pack formats described here
are the stable, documented subset; if the engine evolves, re-check the sources
above.

Anything you find in this guide marked `[OBSERVED]` but not documented upstream
may change between engine versions without notice.


<!-- ===== docs/01-engine-overview.md ===== -->

# 01. Engine Overview

Read this file first. It defines the terminology used by every other document.

## What VoxelCore is

VoxelCore (repo: <https://github.com/MihailRis/voxelcore>) is an open-source voxel
game engine written in C++ with Lua scripting. It ships as an engine binary
(`VoxelEngine` / `VoxelCore`) plus a built-in content pack `base` in `res/content/`.

Game content is **declarative**: blocks, items and most other content are plain
JSON files inside *content packs*. Lua scripts are optional and add behavior on
top of JSON declarations. DO design content as JSON first; add Lua only when the
JSON properties are not enough.

## Core terminology

| Term            | Meaning                                                                 |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Content pack    | A folder containing `package.json` and optional content subfolders.     |
| Pack ID         | The unique identifier declared in `package.json` (`"id"` field).        |
| Block           | A voxel type occupying grid cells in the world (stone, water, torch...).|
| Item            | An inventory object. Every block automatically gets a corresponding item.|
| Content source  | A filesystem path the engine scans for packs (see 02-pack-structure.md).   |
| Mount point     | Internal virtual filesystem entry; each pack gets one named after its ID.|
| Atlas           | A texture collection. Atlases `blocks` and `items` are built from PNGs in the pack's `textures/blocks/` and `textures/items/`. |
| Caption         | Human-readable display name of a block/item shown in the inventory UI.  |

## Namespaced IDs

Almost all content is addressed as `pack_id:content_name` — e.g. `base:dirt`,
`base:grass_block`, `kompot:ui`. Known exceptions exist OUTSIDE blocks/items:
HUD `<image src>` texture names and `menu.page` page names carry NO pack id
(details in 09-hud-and-ui.md).

Rules for IDs (`[VERIFIED]`, identical rules for packs, blocks and items):

- Allowed characters: Latin letters `a-z` `A-Z`, digits `0-9`, underscore `_`.
- MUST NOT start with a digit.
- Length MUST be 2..24 characters inclusive.
- IDs are case-sensitive as written, but DO use lowercase for new content;
  all real packs do.

The special suffix `.item` denotes the item auto-generated for a block:
`base:stone.item` is the item form of block `base:stone`. `[VERIFIED]`
You only need the `.item` form when referencing a block's generated item
explicitly (e.g. in loot tables).

## Reserved names

Pack IDs collide with mount point names, so these are reserved / unavailable for
pack IDs: `res`, `user`, `world`, `project`, `config`, `core`. `core` is an
additional engine-internal pseudo-pack that provides built-in content (e.g. the
empty item `core:empty`). Engine-level tags are namespaced `core:*` (e.g. blocks
carry `"tags": ["core:liquid"]`); packs add their own namespaced tags (the stock
pack tags its ore `base:ore`). `[OBSERVED]`

DO NOT use any of these as pack IDs.

## What a content pack can contain

A minimal pack is **just `package.json`** and it is valid — confirmed
first-hand, nothing else is required. Everything else is optional subfolders:

- `blocks/` — block definitions (JSON) — covered in 03-blocks.md
- `items/` — item definitions (JSON) — covered in 04-items.md
- `textures/` — PNG assets (`textures/blocks/`, `textures/items/`, ...) — covered
  in 05-textures-and-assets.md
- `block_materials/` — interaction material definitions (JSON) — covered in
  05-textures-and-assets.md
- `texts/` — localization files — covered in 05-textures-and-assets.md
- `config/` — TOML config (`defaults.toml`, `bindings.toml`, `user-props.toml`)
  — covered in 02-pack-structure.md
- `layouts/` — UI layouts (XML) — together with `scripts/hud.lua` covered in
  09-hud-and-ui.md
- `package.json`, `icon.png`, `preload.json` — covered in 02-pack-structure.md
- `content.json` — auto-generated by the engine. NEVER create or edit it by hand.
- Excluded topics (defined but NOT documented in this guide): `entities/`,
  `skeletons/`, `models/`, `sounds/`, `shaders/`, `fonts/`, `generators/`,
  `scripts/` (except `hud.lua`), `modules/`, `presets/`, `animation/`. See
  `docs/stubs/` before assuming anything about them. NOTE: the animation folder
  is spelled `animation` (singular) — an upstream quirk baked into the engine
  constant; do NOT "fix" it to `animations`. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`

## How loading works (mental model)

1. The engine scans **content sources** (folders) for subdirectories containing
   a `package.json`.
2. Each discovered pack is registered by the `"id"` from its `package.json`;
   the folder name itself is not the identity, and in real packs it almost
   never equals the ID. `[OBSERVED: pack folder
   kompot_0f9103ff-1.2.2 ships id "kompot" and works]`
3. Dependencies declared in `package.json` are resolved; missing hard
   dependencies fail the load.
4. All enabled packs' content folders (`blocks/`, `items/`, ...) are read and
   every definition is registered into a global, namespaced registry
   (`pack_id:name`).
5. The engine writes/updates each pack's `content.json` (registry index used to
   keep world saves stable across content changes).
6. At runtime, blocks/items referenced anywhere (JSON or Lua) use the
   `pack_id:name` string form; internally they become numeric runtime indices.

Consequences you MUST respect:

- AVOIDs nothing here: removing/renaming content that worlds already contain is
  handled through `content.json` conversion, but renaming IDs still breaks
  references in JSON/Lua and localization. Treat published IDs as immutable.
- The engine does not currently compare pack versions when resolving duplicate
  packs across sources — highest-priority source simply wins. `[DOC]`

## Engine version policy of this guide

This guide is written against the `main` branch state of October 2026 (base pack
version 0.32). It is intentionally not pinned to a commit. If the engine changes
JSON formats, the stock pack `res/content/base/` in the engine repo is always the
authoritative example set — DO re-check it when in doubt.


<!-- ===== docs/02-pack-structure.md ===== -->

# 02. Pack Structure and Manifest

This document defines where packs live, what `package.json` must contain, and
which auxiliary files a pack may have.

## Where packs live (content sources)

The engine discovers packs in **content sources**, scanned in priority order
(highest first). If the same pack ID exists in several sources, the
highest-priority one wins and the rest are ignored. `[VERIFIED]`

| Priority | Source           | Path                                        |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| 1        | `world:content`  | `<world folder>/content/`                   |
| 2        | `user:content`   | `$HOME/.voxeng/content/`                    |
| 3        | `project:content`| `<project folder>/content/` (project mode)  |
| 4        | `res:content`    | `<engine>/res/content/` (built-in packs)    |

Practical guidance:

- For local development DO put your pack into `user:content`:
  `~/.voxeng/content/<pack_id>/` on Linux. This works for any world.
- Packs shipped inside a game project go to `<project>/content/` (see
  07-example-repos.md for a real project doing this).
- `res:content` is for content bundled with the engine build itself (the stock
  `base` pack lives there).

**Folder name vs pack ID.** The engine identifies a pack by the `"id"` inside
`package.json`, NOT by the folder name. The folder name is free-form: real
packs almost always use a folder name different from the ID, and exact matches
are rare in the wild — for example a published project ships a pack in folder
`kompot_0f9103ff-1.2.2` with `"id": "kompot"`, and it loads fine.
`[OBSERVED]` NEVER assume that the folder name equals the pack ID. When you
need a pack's ID, read its `package.json`; when you create a pack folder, any
name works.

## package.json (the only required file)

`[VERIFIED]` Format and field semantics:

```json
{
    "id":          "my_pack",
    "title":       "My Pack",
    "version":     "1.0.0",
    "creator":     "Author Name",
    "description": "What this pack adds",
    "dependencies": ["base", "~randutil@>=1.0"]
}
```

| Field          | Required | Format / notes                                                |
| -------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`           | yes      | Pack ID, rules in 01-engine-overview.md                        |
| `title`        | yes*     | Display name in the content menu                               |
| `version`      | yes*     | `major.minor[.patch]`, e.g. `"1.0"`, `"0.32"`                  |
| `creator`      | no       | Author name; OR use an array field `creators` instead `[DOC]`  |
| `description`  | no       | Short free-form text                                           |
| `dependencies` | no       | Array of dependency strings (see below)                        |
| `license`      | no       | Observed in real packs (`"license": "MPL-2.0"`); engine ignores unknown fields `[OBSERVED]` |

\* Official docs show `title`/`version` in every example; packs without them are
unknown territory. DO always include `id`, `title`, `version`.

### Dependencies

Each dependency string is `[prefix]pack_id[@version_spec]`:

| Prefix | Meaning      | Behavior                                                        |
| ------ | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `!` or none | required | Pack fails to load without it (this is the default) `[DOC]`     |
| `?`    | optional     | Loaded if present, ignored otherwise                            |
| `~`    | weak         | Order-only / best-effort (documented as "weak dependency")      |

Version spec operators exist (e.g. `>=1.0`, `*` = any, which is the default).
Only `>=` is shown by official docs; AVOID inventing other operators (`<`, `=`)
— they are not documented. `[VERIFIED: 'randutil@>=1.0' example]`

Real examples:

- Stock `base` pack has **no dependencies**:
  `{ "id": "base", "title": "Base", "version": "0.32", "description": "basic content package" }`
- Real pack: `"dependencies": ["kompot"]` (hard dependency on the Kompot UI pack).

**DO declare a dependency on `"base"` if your pack uses `base:*` properties**
such as `base:durability` or `base:loot` — those are user-defined properties
registered by the `base` pack, not engine built-ins (see 03-blocks.md).

## icon.png

- Optional file at the **pack root** (NOT inside `textures/`). `[VERIFIED]`
- Recommended size 128x128 `[DOC]`; the stock pack ships 64x64 and a real pack
  ships 210x208, so the size is clearly not enforced. `[OBSERVED]`
- DO keep it square PNG.

## Folder layout

Full layout documented upstream, annotated with this guide's scope. A minimal
pack only needs `package.json`; create subfolders only when you actually define
content.

```text
my_pack/
├── package.json            # REQUIRED manifest
├── icon.png                # optional, pack root
├── blocks/                 # IN SCOPE  — 03-blocks.md
├── items/                  # IN SCOPE  — 04-items.md
├── block_materials/        # IN SCOPE  — 05-textures-and-assets.md
├── textures/
│   ├── blocks/             # IN SCOPE — auto-joins the global "blocks" atlas
│   └── items/              # IN SCOPE — auto-joins the global "items" atlas
├── texts/                  # IN SCOPE  — localization (05)
├── preload.json            # IN SCOPE  — 05-textures-and-assets.md
├── config/                 # partially in scope — see below
├── content.json            # AUTO-GENERATED. NEVER hand-edit, NEVER create.
├── entities/               # OUT OF SCOPE (stub)
├── skeletons/              # OUT OF SCOPE (stub)
├── models/                 # OUT OF SCOPE (stub)
├── sounds/                 # OUT OF SCOPE (stub)
├── shaders/                # OUT OF SCOPE
├── fonts/                  # OUT OF SCOPE
├── animation/              # OUT OF SCOPE (stub) — singular spelling, NOT "animations"
├── layouts/                # IN SCOPE (HUD/UI basics) — 09-hud-and-ui.md
├── generators/             # OUT OF SCOPE (stub: worldgen)
├── scripts/                # OUT OF SCOPE (Lua) — EXCEPT scripts/hud.lua (09)
├── modules/                # OUT OF SCOPE (Lua libraries)
├── presets/                # OUT OF SCOPE
├── devtools/               # OUT OF SCOPE
├── resources.json          # engine resources (cameras, effects) — rare, skip
└── resource-aliases.json   # resource aliases — rare, skip
```

`config/` subfolder:

- `config/defaults.toml` — overrides default content bindings of the game:
  the stock pack sets
  ```toml
  generator = "base:demo"
  player-entity = "base:player"
  hand-skeleton = "base:hand"
  block-material = "base:stone"
  ```
  `[OBSERVED]` Only relevant for total-conversion-style packs; typical add-on
  packs do not ship this file.
- `config/bindings.toml` — key bindings declared by the pack. Real format:
  ```toml
  [kompot]
  gallery = "key:f12"
  ```
  i.e. `[pack_id]` section, `action_name = "key:<code>"`. `[OBSERVED]`
- `config/user-props.toml` — declares custom properties the pack adds to
  blocks/items. Real example from `base`:
  ```toml
  "base:durability" = {}
  "base:loot" = {}
  ```
  `[VERIFIED]` Custom properties are then read at runtime via Lua
  (`block.properties[id]["prop"]`) — scripting, out of scope here.

## Enabling a pack for a world

- Normal mode: enable the pack in the engine's content menu when
  creating/configuring a world (UI flow, not file-driven). Dependencies are
  enabled automatically.
- Project mode: a `project.toml` at the project root lists default packs:
  ```toml
  base_packs = ["base", "kompot", "wooden_meat_menu"]
  ```
  `[OBSERVED]` (from the wooden_meat_game project). Projects themselves are out
  of scope — see docs/stubs/TODO-projects.md.

## DO / AVOID summary

- DO make the minimal pack first (`package.json` only), verify it loads, then add content.
- DO treat the folder name as free-form; NEVER assume it must match the pack
  ID (real packs rarely match — the ID lives only in `package.json`).
- DO put `icon.png` at pack root, not in `textures/`.
- DO declare `dependencies` when you reference `base:*` or any other pack's content.
- AVOID editing `content.json` — it is generated; manual edits corrupt worlds (upstream warning).
- AVOID version specs other than the documented `>=` form.
- AVOID relying on pack `version` for resolution — content sources ignore versions entirely. `[DOC]`


<!-- ===== docs/03-blocks.md ===== -->

# 03. Blocks Reference

Block definitions are JSON files in `blocks/` of the pack. The file name defines
the content name: `blocks/dirt.json` in pack `base` becomes `base:dirt`.
`[VERIFIED]` ID rules: see 01-engine-overview.md.

A block file can be almost empty — every property has a default. The minimal
sensible block is:

```json
{ "texture": "stone" }
```

Full real example from the stock pack (`base:grass_block`, comments added here,
JSON itself is comment-free):

```json
{
    "material": "base:grass_block",
    "texture-faces": [
        "grass_side",      // index 0: -X (west)
        "grass_side",      // index 1: +X (east)
        "dirt",            // index 2: -Y (bottom)
        "grass_top",       // index 3: +Y (top)
        "grass_side",      // index 4: -Z (north)
        "grass_side"       // index 5: +Z (south)
    ],
    "base:durability": 1.7,
    "base:loot": [
        {"item": "base:dirt.item"}
    ]
}
```

## Texture properties

### `texture` — single texture for all faces

Texture NAME only: no path, no `.png` extension. The PNG must be in the pack's
`textures/blocks/` folder. `[VERIFIED]` Example: `"texture": "dirt"` resolves to
`<pack>/textures/blocks/dirt.png` and lands in the global `blocks` atlas.

### `texture-faces` — per-face textures

Array of exactly 6 texture names, order:

| Index | Face        | Direction |
| ----- | ----------- | --------- |
| 0     | west        | −X        |
| 1     | east        | +X        |
| 2     | bottom      | −Y        |
| 3     | top         | +Y        |
| 4     | north       | −Z        |
| 5     | south       | +Z        |

`[VERIFIED]` against engine face constants (`FACE_MX, FACE_PX, FACE_MY, FACE_PY,
FACE_MZ, FACE_PZ` in `src/voxels/Block.hpp`) and the stock `grass_block.json`.
This order is NOT stated in official docs — it was extracted from source + real
files. Fewer than 6 elements is a hard load error. `[OBSERVED: engine throws]`

- `texture` and `texture-faces` are mutually exclusive. `[DOC — IMPORTANT]`

### `overlay-texture`

Seen in stock `water.json` (`"overlay-texture": "blocks:water"`); value is an
atlas reference (`atlas:name`). Not documented upstream. `[OBSERVED]`

## Model properties

### `model` — built-in model type

| Value    | Behavior                                                              |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `block`  | Default full cube (default for all blocks)                             |
| `none`   | Invisible block (air-like)                                             |
| `X`      | Two crossed sprites — grass/flowers style (see `flower.json` example)  |
| `aabb`   | Mesh matches the block hitbox (pipes, torch, doors, lamps)             |
| `custom` | Requires `model-name` (custom model file) — OUT OF SCOPE, see stubs    |

`[VERIFIED]`

### `model-name` — custom model file

Value is a model name without the `<pack>:models/` prefix and without extension.
Custom models are an excluded topic (docs/stubs/TODO-models.md). Textures used
inside custom models must live in the `blocks` atlas and be referenced as
`blocks:name`. `[DOC]`

### `draw-group` — integer

Render group number. Relevant for translucent blocks (water uses `3`, sprites
like flowers use `1`) to fix invisible-face sorting issues. `[VERIFIED]`

### `translucent` — boolean

Enables alpha translucency of the texture (water, ice). Costs performance; NOT
needed for full transparency (leaves, flowers) and NOT needed with `draw-group`
alone. `[DOC]`

### `solid` — boolean

Declares a `custom`-model block as fully solid so hidden-face culling works like
for `block` cubes. Ignored when `false`. `[DOC]`

### `culling` — `"default"` | `"optional"` | `"disabled"`

Face culling mode within a draw group. `[DOC]`

### `shadeless` — boolean

Disables lighting on the block model (torch flame uses it). `[VERIFIED]`

### `ambient-occlusion` — boolean (default true)

Vertex ambient occlusion toggle. `[VERIFIED]`

## Rotation

### `rotation` — placement rotation profile

| Value     | For blocks like            |
| --------- | -------------------------- |
| `none`    | default; no rotation       |
| `pipe`    | logs, pipes, torches (axis alignment) |
| `pane`    | panels, doors, signs (flat alignment) |
| `stairs`  | stairs (`pane` + upside-down variants) |
| `ladder`  | ladders (`pipe` on vertical + `pane` on horizontal surfaces) |

`[DOC]` Real usage: `wood.json` and `torch.json` use `"rotation": "pipe"`,
`wooden_door.json` uses `"pane"`. `[OBSERVED]`

## Lighting

### `emission` — `[R, G, B]`, each 0..15

Light emitted by the block. `[15,15,15]` = brightest white; `[0,0,0]` (default) =
no emission. `[VERIFIED]` Example: stock lamp: `"emission": [15, 14, 13]`,
torch: `"emission": [13, 10, 2]`.

### `light-passing` — boolean

Block lets light from emitters pass through. Flowers, torch, water, glass set it. `[VERIFIED]`

### `sky-light-passing` — boolean

Block does not block the vertical sunbeam. Water explicitly sets `false`
(so it darkens underwater). `[VERIFIED]`

## Physics

### `obstacle` — boolean (default true)

`false` removes the hitbox — players walk through (flowers, water, torch). `[VERIFIED]`

### `hitbox` — `[x, y, z, w, h, d]`, all in 0..1

Offset + size of the hitbox inside the block cell. Example from `torch.json`:
`[0.4375, 0.0, 0.4375, 0.125, 0.5, 0.125]` = small stick in the middle.
`[VERIFIED]` Axis semantics: +X=east, +Y=up, +Z=south (from upstream docs of the
hitbox example). For multiple boxes use `hitboxes` with an array of such arrays
(stock door uses it). `[VERIFIED]`

### `grounded` — boolean

Block must be placed on a full block and breaks when support breaks (flowers,
torch). `[VERIFIED]`

### `selectable` — boolean (default true)

`false` — the cursor targets blocks behind it (water). `[VERIFIED]`

### `replaceable` — boolean

`true` — placing any block replaces this one (water, grass, flowers). `[VERIFIED]`

### `breakable` — boolean (default true)

`false` — block cannot be broken. `[DOC]`

### `size` — `[sx, sy, sz]` integers, default `[1,1,1]`

Extended (multi-cell) blocks; the stock door is `"size": [1, 2, 1]`. `[VERIFIED]`
With `grounded` on extended blocks, `grounding-behaviour` picks which segments
need support: `partial` (default) / `complete` / `origin`. `[DOC]`

## Inventory & interaction

### `caption` — display name

Human-readable name. Blocks normally skip it: the default caption is derived
from the ID with underscores turned into spaces (`grass_block` → `grass block`),
and the engine upper-cases it for display. Localization then maps caption
strings (see 05). The stock pack sets `"caption": "tall grass"` only where the
auto name is wrong. `[OBSERVED]`

### `hidden` — boolean

Hides the block from inventory and suppresses auto-generated item; upstream
docs say from engine 0.17+ such blocks MUST define `picking-item`. `[DOC]`

### `picking-item` — item ID

Item given by middle-click pick. Stock example: hidden `door:door_open` sets
`"picking-item": "door:door.item"`. `[DOC]`

### `inventory-size` — integer (default 0)

Slots of the block's own inventory (containers). UI hookup is an excluded topic. `[DOC]`

### `ui-layout` — layout ID for the block's UI. Excluded topic. `[DOC]`

## Materials (interaction sounds)

### `material` — `pack:material_name`

References a definition in `block_materials/` that maps to step/place/break/hit
sounds. See 05-textures-and-assets.md for the material file format. Stock
examples: `"material": "base:wood"`, `"base:ground"`, `"base:glass"`. `[VERIFIED]`

## Data & scripting hooks (short)

- `fields` — typed per-block data slots (int8..int64, float32/64, char; total
  ≤ 240 bytes; array `length` supported; `convert-strategy`: `reset`/`clamp`).
  `[DOC]` Useful only together with Lua — see stubs before using.
- `state-based` — variant table switching `model`/`model-name`/`texture`/
  `texture-faces` by user bits (`offset`, `bits`, `variants`, max 16 variants).
  `[DOC]` Controlled from Lua via `block.set_variant(x, y, z, index)`.
- `script-name` — script file name (without `pack:scripts/` and extension) that
  holds this block's event handlers. Default: the block's own name. `[DOC]`
- `tick-interval` — world ticks (1/20 s) between `on_block_tick` events. `[DOC]`
- `properties@append` — any list property can be suffixed with `@append` by
  *other packs* to extend instead of overwrite. `[DOC]`

## Tags

`"tags": ["core:liquid", ...]` — free-form labels; prefix them with a namespace
to avoid collisions. The engine uses the `core:*` namespace (stock water block:
`"tags": ["core:liquid"]`); the stock pack namespaces its own tags as `base:ore`
(coal ore). `[VERIFIED]` Other packs can tag your content from their own
`tags.toml` file:

```toml
"my_pack:gemlike" = ["some_pack:some_ore", "my_pack:ruby_ore"]
"my_pack:flammable" = ["my_pack:wooden_floor"]
```

## Properties registered by the `base` pack (not engine built-ins!)

- `base:durability` — seconds to break without tools. Stock: dirt 1.5,
  grass_block 1.7, stone 12.0, wood 6.0, flower 0.0. `[VERIFIED]`
- `base:loot` — array of `{ "item": "pack:item", "count": n | "min": n, "max": m, "chance": p }`.
  `item` MUST be an ITEM id — for a block's item form append `.item`
  (`"base:dirt.item"`). `chance` default 1.0. `[VERIFIED]`
- Drop semantics observed in the stock pack: blocks WITHOUT `base:loot` (stone,
  dirt) drop their own generated item when broken; `"base:loot": []` (tall
  grass) means drop nothing. `[OBSERVED]`
- Using either REQUIRES a dependency on `"base"` (02-pack-structure.md).

## Observed-but-undocumented properties

- `surface-replacement` — stock `dirt.json` sets `"surface-replacement": "base:grass_block"`;
  grass spreading to exposed dirt is implemented via this + the block script's
  `on_random_update`. Semantics are not documented upstream. `[OBSERVED]`
- `overlay-texture` — see Texture properties. `[OBSERVED]`
- Block-level `caption` — see above. `[OBSERVED]`

DO NOT rely on undocumented properties for anything critical; prefer documented
equivalents and check the stock pack again when the engine updates.

## Annotated stock examples

`base:dirt` — minimal solid cube with base-pack props:

```json
{
    "texture": "dirt",
    "material": "base:ground",
    "surface-replacement": "base:grass_block",
    "base:durability": 1.5
}
```

`base:flower` — crossed sprite, no collision, replaceable, no loot:

```json
{
    "texture": "flower",
    "material": "base:grass",
    "draw-group": 1,
    "light-passing": true,
    "obstacle": false,
    "replaceable": true,
    "grounded": true,
    "model": "X",
    "hitbox": [0.15, 0.0, 0.15, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7],
    "base:durability": 0.0
}
```

`base:water` — translucent liquid:

```json
{
    "texture": "water",
    "overlay-texture": "blocks:water",
    "draw-group": 3,
    "light-passing": true,
    "sky-light-passing": false,
    "obstacle": false,
    "selectable": false,
    "replaceable": true,
    "translucent": true,
    "tags": ["core:liquid"]
}
```

`base:torch` — `aabb` model, light, particles, rotation:

```json
{
    "texture-faces": ["torch_side","torch_side","torch_bottom","torch_top","torch_side","torch_side"],
    "emission": [13, 10, 2],
    "model": "aabb",
    "hitbox": [0.4375, 0.0, 0.4375, 0.125, 0.5, 0.125],
    "light-passing": true,
    "shadeless": true,
    "obstacle": false,
    "grounded": true,
    "rotation": "pipe",
    "material": "base:wood",
    "base:durability": 0.1
}
```
(`particles` object shortened; particle configs are an excluded topic.)

## DO / AVOID summary

- DO start every block JSON with `texture` or `texture-faces`; add the rest as needed.
- DO give `texture-faces` exactly 6 entries in the west/east/bottom/top/north/south order.
- DO use `"model": "X"` + `obstacle:false` + `replaceable:true` + `grounded:true` + `draw-group:1` for plants.
- DO reference block-derived items with the `.item` suffix in loot/pick properties.
- AVOID combining `texture` with `texture-faces` in one block.
- AVOID `translucent` unless you need alpha blending (prefer `draw-group` + `light-passing`).
- AVOID inventing property names; everything allowed is listed above or in upstream docs.
- AVOID depending on `[OBSERVED]` properties without a fallback plan.


<!-- ===== docs/04-items.md ===== -->

# 04. Items Reference

Item definitions are JSON files in `items/` of the pack. The file name defines
the content name: `items/shotgun.json` in pack `my_pack` becomes
`my_pack:shotgun`. `[VERIFIED]`

Every block also automatically gets an item — addressed as
`<pack>:<block_name>.item` — which places the block on right-click. DO NOT
create `items/<name>.json` for a block that already exists; that suffix form is
for *referencing* the generated item, not a file path.

## Real annotated examples

Stock pack, `base:bazalt_breaker` (a tool-like item):

```json
{
    "icon-type": "sprite",
    "icon": "items:bazalt_breaker",
    "uses": 100
}
```

Real game pack, `my_pack:shotgun` (wooden_meat_game):

```json
{
    "icon-type": "sprite",
    "icon": "items:shotgun",
    "stack-size": 1,
    "model-name": "shotgun"
}
```
`model-name: "shotgun"` resolves to `my_pack:models/shotgun.obj` — models are an
excluded topic (docs/stubs/TODO-models.md); omitting `model-name` makes the
engine generate a default model.

Real game pack, `my_pack:spawn_nepis` (spawn-egg style item driven by a script):

```json
{
    "icon-type": "sprite",
    "icon": "items:nepis"
}
```

## Property reference

### Visual

| Property     | Type   | Meaning                                                                 |
| ------------ | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `icon-type`  | string | `sprite` (2D icon) \| `block` (3D block preview). `none` exists only for `core:empty` and may be removed — AVOID using it. `[DOC]` |
| `icon`       | string | For `sprite`: `atlas:texture` — e.g. `items:shotgun`, `blocks:dirt`. For `block`: block ID — e.g. `base:wood`. `[VERIFIED]` |
| `model-name` | string | Item model name; default `packid:itemname`; auto-generated when absent. `[DOC]` |
| `caption`    | string | Display name in inventory. Supports inline `md` markup. `[DOC]` Default caption derives from the ID (underscores → spaces). `[OBSERVED]` |
| `description`| string | Inventory tooltip. Supports inline `md` markup. `[DOC]` |

The two automatic atlases are `blocks` (from `textures/blocks/*.png`) and
`items` (from `textures/items/*.png`) — same for every pack; your PNGs simply
join them by file name. See 05-textures-and-assets.md.

### Behavior

| Property        | Type    | Meaning                                                                 |
| --------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `placing-block` | string  | Block ID placed on right-click. This is what generated block-items use internally. `[DOC]` |
| `emission`      | [R,G,B] | Light emitted while held in hand, each channel 0..15. `[DOC]`            |
| `stack-size`    | int     | Max per inventory slot. Default 64. Shotgun uses 1. `[VERIFIED]`         |
| `uses`          | int     | Durability/consumable counter, driven via `inventory.use()` from Lua. Shown in inventory UI. `[VERIFIED]` |
| `uses-display`  | string  | `none` \| `number` \| `relation` \| `vbar` (default `vbar`). `[DOC]`     |
| `script-name`   | string  | Script file (without `pack:scripts/` and extension) with the item's event handlers. Default: the item's own name. `[DOC]` |

### Tags

`"tags": ["core:fuel", "my_pack:gems"]` — same rules as block tags: namespaced,
`core:*` reserved for the engine. `[VERIFIED]` Other packs may tag your items
from their `tags.toml`.

### Item scripts (boundary knowledge only)

An item whose JSON has no `placing-block` usually gets behavior from a Lua
script `scripts/<script-name>.lua`. Event handlers are global Lua functions, e.g.
`function on_use(pid)` — the stock pack's `bazalt_breaker.lua` and the game's
`shotgun.lua` both define `on_use(pid)`. `[OBSERVED]` The full event/API list is
a Lua-scripting topic: NOT covered here — read `doc/ru/scripting.md` +
`doc/ru/scripting/` in the engine repo before writing item scripts.

## Localization of captions

Caption strings are looked up in the pack's `texts/<locale>.txt` files
(`key=value` per line). The stock pack translates `"bazalt breaker"` (the
auto-derived caption of `bazalt_breaker`) in `ru_RU.txt` as
`bazalt breaker=крушитель базальта`. `[VERIFIED]` Details in 05.

## DO / AVOID summary

- DO give every item an explicit `icon-type: "sprite"` + `icon: "items:<name>"`.
- DO ship a 16x16 PNG at `textures/items/<name>.png` for each sprite icon.
- DO use `placing-block` if you want an item that places an existing block under
  a different identity/name.
- DO use `stack-size: 1` for tools/weapons.
- AVOID creating an item file duplicating a block (`base:dirt.item` already exists).
- AVOID `icon-type: "none"` — documented as removable, used only by `core:empty`.
- AVOID referencing atlas textures with paths or `.png` extensions — only `atlas:name`.
- AVOID guessing item event handler names beyond `on_use(pid)` without checking
  the engine's scripting docs.


<!-- ===== docs/05-textures-and-assets.md ===== -->

# 05. Textures, Atlases, preload.json, Materials, Localization

This document covers the asset side of the IN-SCOPE topics: block/item textures,
the pack icon, asset preloading, block materials, and caption localization.

## Texture folders and atlases

Two global texture atlases exist and every pack contributes to them
automatically: `[VERIFIED]`

| Atlas    | Fed by                       | Used for                          |
| -------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `blocks` | `<pack>/textures/blocks/*.png` | block `texture`/`texture-faces`, block-model textures |
| `items`  | `<pack>/textures/items/*.png`  | item sprite icons (`icon: "items:x"`) |

Rules:

- Texture NAME = file name without `.png`. `"texture": "dirt"` →
  `textures/blocks/dirt.png` → atlas entry `blocks:dirt`. `[VERIFIED]`
- Stock pack textures are 16x16 RGBA PNG. DO use 16x16 (or a consistent power
  of two) — mixed sizes across packs are untested territory. `[OBSERVED]`
- AVOID referencing textures by path or with `.png` — always `atlas:name`.
- Name collisions between packs in the same atlas are not documented; DO prefix
  file names with something pack-specific when genericity is likely
  (`mymod_gear.png` instead of `gear.png`). `[OBSERVED-CONCERN]`

Additional pack textures (GUI, particles, sky) are loaded only through
`preload.json` `"textures"` — plain paths relative to `textures/` without
extension, e.g. `"gui/crosshair"` from `<pack>/textures/gui/crosshair.png`.
`[VERIFIED: stock preload.json]`

Custom atlases: `preload.json` accepts an `"atlases"` array, e.g. stock pack:
`"atlases": [{"name": "cracks", "type": "separate"}]` (folder
`textures/cracks/`); the Kompot pack registers atlases `kompot_ui_icons` /
`kompot_ui_skin`. Custom atlas machinery is UI/advanced territory — out of
scope. `[OBSERVED]`

## Pack icon

`icon.png` at the pack root, square PNG, recommended 128x128 `[DOC]`; existing
packs range from 64x64 to 210x208 and load fine `[OBSERVED]`.

## preload.json

Optional file at pack root preloading assets the engine would not load on
demand. Format: object whose keys are asset categories, values are arrays of
asset names/paths (no extensions). `[VERIFIED]`

Categories: `animation`, `fonts`, `models`, `shaders`, `skeletons`, `sounds`,
`textures`. Extras seen in real packs: `atlases` (see above). `[OBSERVED]`

```json
{
    "atlases": [{"name": "cracks", "type": "separate"}],
    "sounds":  ["blocks/door_open", "events/pickup"],
    "models":  ["drop-item"],
    "textures": ["misc/moon", "misc/sun", "gui/crosshair"]
}
```

Real game-pack example (wooden_meat_game / my_pack):

```json
{
    "animation": ["hit", "rip"],
    "sounds": ["shotgun"],
    "textures": ["gfx/muzzle_flash", "gfx/tracer"]
}
```

Sound names load all variant files by pattern: `sound_name.ogg`,
`sound_name_1.ogg`, `sound_name_2.ogg`, ... or `sound_name_0.ogg`, ... `[DOC]`

Fonts entries are objects `{"name": "kompot_12", "path": "fonts/IBMPlexSans-Regular.ttf", "size": 12}` `[OBSERVED]`.

AVOID preloading things you do not use — upstream docs explicitly warn against
unnecessary preload entries. `[DOC]`

## Block materials (`block_materials/`)

A *material* bundles interaction sounds for blocks. Blocks reference it by
`"material": "pack:material_name"`; files are JSON in `block_materials/`
(`block_materials/wood.json` → `base:wood`). `[VERIFIED]`

```json
{
    "steps-sound": "steps/wood",
    "place-sound": "blocks/wood_place",
    "break-sound": "blocks/wood_break",
    "hit-sound": "blocks/wood_hit",
    "sound-absorption": 0.5
}
```

- Sound values are names resolved against loaded sounds (sounds themselves are
  an EXCLUDED topic — docs/stubs/TODO-sounds.md; the stock sounds live in the
  `base` pack).
- The stock `config/defaults.toml` sets `block-material = "base:stone"` as the
  game-wide fallback. `[OBSERVED]`
- DO reuse existing `base:*` materials (`base:stone`, `base:wood`, `base:ground`,
  `base:glass`, `base:grass`, `base:metal`, ...) instead of creating duplicates.
- AVOID creating a material with sound names that no loaded pack provides.

## Localization (`texts/`)

Files named by locale: `en_US.txt`, `ru_RU.txt`, `fi_FI.txt`, `uk_UA.txt`,
`uz_UZ.txt` are all observed in real packs. `[VERIFIED]`

Format — one `key=value` pair per line. Content captions use the caption string
itself as the key: `[VERIFIED]`

```text
# ru_RU.txt of the base pack (excerpt)
dirt=земля
grass block=дёрн
bazalt breaker=крушитель базальта
```

- Caption keys match the lowercased caption (the engine auto-capitalizes for
  display; docs recommend NOT capitalizing captions yourself). `[DOC]`
- UI-level translations use dotted keys, e.g. `kompot.gallery=Kompot / Gallery`
  in the Kompot pack. `[OBSERVED]`
- DO provide `en_US.txt` only for entries that differ from the caption itself;
  captions are already the English defaults.

## DO / AVOID summary

- DO drop every block texture into `textures/blocks/<name>.png` and every item
  icon into `textures/items/<name>.png` — nothing else needed for them to work.
- DO keep textures 16x16 RGBA PNG for blocks/items.
- DO reference textures as `blocks:name` / `items:name` everywhere.
- DO preload only what is not auto-loaded (extra textures, sounds, models).
- AVOID `.png` extensions and folder paths inside `texture`/`icon` values.
- AVOID editing preload entries for auto-loaded assets (blocks/items atlas
  textures do not need preload).
- AVOID translating by editing captions per language — captions stay in English;
  translations go to `texts/<locale>.txt`.


<!-- ===== docs/06-walkthrough.md ===== -->

# 06. Walkthrough: Build a Complete Minimal Pack

Goal: a working pack `my_first_pack` that adds:
- block `my_first_pack:ruby_ore` — a stone-like ore cube,
- block `my_first_pack:ruby_lamp` — a glowing cube,
- block `my_first_pack:ruby_flower` — a decorative plant,
- item `my_first_pack:ruby` — a plain sprite item,
- a pack icon.

No Lua, no models, no sounds — pure declarative content. Every file below is
complete and final; assemble them in order and the pack works.

## Step 0 — Choose the location

DO develop in the user content folder so any world can use the pack:

```text
$HOME/.voxeng/content/my_first_pack/
```

(Linux path; `user:content` source, priority above `res:content` — see
02-pack-structure.md.) The folder name is free-form — it does NOT need to
match the pack ID (real packs rarely match). This walkthrough uses the ID as
the folder name purely for tidiness.

## Step 1 — package.json (pack becomes loadable)

File: `my_first_pack/package.json`

```json
{
    "id": "my_first_pack",
    "title": "My First Pack",
    "version": "0.1.0",
    "creator": "Your Name",
    "description": "Ruby ore, lamp, flower and a ruby item",
    "dependencies": ["base"]
}
```

`dependencies: ["base"]` is REQUIRED here because the blocks below use
`base:durability` and `base:loot` (properties registered by `base`).

STOP and verify: the pack must already appear in the engine's content menu with
no other files at all.

## Step 2 — Textures

Create two folders and four PNG files, 16x16, RGBA:

```text
textures/blocks/ruby_ore.png
textures/blocks/ruby_lamp.png
textures/blocks/ruby_flower.png
textures/items/ruby.png
```

Any 16x16 pixel-art works while prototyping. The file names become the texture
names (`ruby_ore`, ...). No `.json` needed for textures — the atlases pick PNGs
up automatically (see 05).

## Step 3 — The ore block

File: `blocks/ruby_ore.json`

```json
{
    "texture": "ruby_ore",
    "material": "base:stone",
    "base:durability": 3.0,
    "base:loot": [
        {"item": "my_first_pack:ruby", "min": 1, "max": 2, "chance": 1.0}
    ]
}
```

Notes:
- `"texture"` — single texture on all 6 faces (order not relevant here).
- `"material": "base:stone"` — reuses base's sounds; no sound files needed.
- loot drops the ITEM `my_first_pack:ruby` defined in Step 6.

## Step 4 — The lamp block

File: `blocks/ruby_lamp.json`

```json
{
    "texture": "ruby_lamp",
    "material": "base:glass",
    "emission": [14, 4, 4],
    "light-passing": true,
    "base:durability": 0.5
}
```

`emission` channels are 0..15; `[14, 4, 4]` is strong red. This block drops
itself when broken: blocks without `base:loot` default to dropping their own
generated item (stock stone/dirt behave this way `[OBSERVED]`).

## Step 5 — The flower block (crossed sprite)

File: `blocks/ruby_flower.json`

```json
{
    "texture": "ruby_flower",
    "material": "base:grass",
    "model": "X",
    "draw-group": 1,
    "light-passing": true,
    "obstacle": false,
    "replaceable": true,
    "grounded": true,
    "hitbox": [0.15, 0.0, 0.15, 0.7, 0.5, 0.7],
    "base:durability": 0.0,
    "base:loot": []
}
```

This is the stock flower recipe: `model X` + no obstacle + replaceable + grounded
+ draw-group 1. `"base:loot": []` means it drops nothing (vs. default self-drop).

## Step 6 — The ruby item

File: `items/ruby.json`

```json
{
    "icon-type": "sprite",
    "icon": "items:ruby",
    "stack-size": 64
}
```

`"icon": "items:ruby"` points at `textures/items/ruby.png` from Step 2. This
item is inert (no `placing-block`, no script) — it is a material/crafting-style
resource.

## Step 7 — Pack icon

Save a square PNG as `icon.png` at the pack root (128x128 recommended).

## Step 8 — Enable and test

1. Launch the engine.
2. Create or open a world; open the content selection and enable
   **My First Pack** (its dependency `base` is required for any world anyway).
3. In game: give items through the inventory/content screen, place the ore,
   break it — the ruby item drops; place the lamp — the area lights red; place
   the flower on top of a full block.

## Final file tree

```text
my_first_pack/
├── package.json
├── icon.png
├── blocks/
│   ├── ruby_ore.json
│   ├── ruby_lamp.json
│   └── ruby_flower.json
├── items/
│   └── ruby.json
└── textures/
    ├── blocks/
    │   ├── ruby_ore.png
    │   ├── ruby_lamp.png
    │   └── ruby_flower.png
    └── items/
        └── ruby.png
```

(`content.json` appears next to `package.json` after the pack loads — generated
by the engine. AVOID touching it.)

## Extensions beyond this walkthrough

- Per-face textures → `texture-faces` (03-blocks.md).
- Localization of captions → `texts/ru_RU.txt` with `ruby ore=рубиновая руда`
  (05-textures-and-assets.md).
- Behavior (drop-on-use, ticking) → Lua scripts, out of scope; see stubs and
  then the engine's `doc/ru/scripting.md`.

## Verification checklist

- [ ] `package.json` parses as JSON (no trailing commas, no comments).
- [ ] `id` passes the character/length rules and is not reserved (the folder
      name may be anything — equality with `id` is not required).
- [ ] Every `texture`/`icon` name has a matching PNG in the right folder.
- [ ] Every `pack:` reference points to an existing pack (dependency declared).
- [ ] `base:*` properties are used only with `"base"` in dependencies.
- [ ] No `content.json` in your source files (engine generates it).


<!-- ===== docs/07-example-repos.md ===== -->

# 07. Annotated Breakdown of Real Repositories

Two real-world repositories are referenced by this guide. Read this file to map
their structure onto the concepts, and to know which of their folders are OUT OF
SCOPE of this guide.

- Game project: <https://github.com/George-Noise/wooden_meat_game>
- UI pack: <https://github.com/George-Noise/fork_of_kompot>

Both are unfinished but load and run; they are referenced as *structure
evidence*, not as style guides.

## wooden_meat_game — a game project wrapping several packs

Top level is a **project**, not a pack (projects are an excluded topic — see
docs/stubs/TODO-projects-worldgen.md):

```text
wooden_meat_game/
├── project.toml            # project manifest
├── project_client.lua      # project-level client script   (out of scope)
├── start.lua               # project entry script           (out of scope)
├── voxelcore_types.lua     # Lua type annotations           (out of scope)
└── content/                # project:content source — packs live here
```

`project.toml`:

```toml
name = "wooden_meat_game"
title = "Wooden Meat Game"
base_packs = ["base", "kompot", "wooden_meat_menu"]
permissions = []
```

`base_packs` lists packs enabled by default; they resolve against
`project:content` (this repo's `content/`) and lower-priority sources.
`[OBSERVED]`

### Packs inside content/

| Folder                      | id in package.json | Lesson                                              |
| --------------------------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `kompot_0f9103ff-1.2.2/`    | `kompot`           | **Folder name ≠ pack ID** — engine reads the ID from package.json `[OBSERVED]` |
| `my_pack/`                  | `my_pack`          | Title differs from id: "Simple Box and Gun" — fine  |
| `sfx/`                      | `vd_ambient_sfx`   | Folder `sfx`, id `vd_ambient_sfx` — again ≠         |
| `vd_belt_system/`           | `vd_belt_system`   | Conventional 1:1 naming (recommended default)       |
| `wooden_meat_menu/`         | `wooden_meat_menu` | Declares `"dependencies": ["kompot"]` `[OBSERVED]`  |

Vendored-pack naming (`kompot_<hash>-<version>`) is a human-organization trick;
the engine only sees id `kompot`.

### my_pack — what is in scope

```text
my_pack/
├── package.json            # id "my_pack", version "0.0.1"
├── icon.png                # 210x208 — icon size is not enforced
├── content.json            # auto-generated (items/entities lists)
├── items/
│   ├── shotgun.json
│   ├── spawn_nepis.json
│   └── spawn_turret.json
├── textures/
│   └── items/              # shotgun.png, nepis.png, turret.png → items atlas
├── preload.json
├── scripts/ ...            # Lua event handlers (out of scope)
├── entities/ ...           # out of scope
├── models/ ...             # out of scope
├── animation/, skeletons/, sounds/   # out of scope
```

`package.json` has no `dependencies` yet references only its own content —
correct, because it does not use `base:*` properties.

`items/shotgun.json`:

```json
{
  "icon-type": "sprite",
  "icon": "items:shotgun",
  "stack-size": 1,
  "model-name": "shotgun"
}
```

Takeaways (all `[OBSERVED]`):
- Sprite icon `"items:shotgun"` ↔ file `textures/items/shotgun.png`.
- `stack-size: 1` for a weapon; `model-name: "shotgun"` pulls
  `models/shotgun.obj`.
- `items/spawn_nepis.json` has only `icon-type`+`icon` — the rest of behavior
  lives in `scripts/spawn_nepis.lua` (handler `on_use(pid)`, spawns an entity).
- `preload.json` preloads only non-auto assets, with keys `animation` (NOTE the
  singular spelling — engine constant), `sounds`, `textures`: two animations,
  one sound, two effect textures (see 05).
- Note the absence of `blocks/` — a pack is NOT required to define blocks.

## fork_of_kompot — a pack distributing a Lua framework

Kompot is a declarative-UI framework pack ("Jetpack-Compose-like") distributed
AS a content pack. Kompot's own framework internals stay out of scope, but the
engine-side HUD/UI mechanics its files use (`scripts/hud.lua`, `layouts/`,
`config/bindings.toml`) are now covered in 09-hud-and-ui.md. `[OBSERVED]`
throughout.

```text
fork_of_kompot/
├── package.json            # id "kompot", version "1.2.2", "license": "MPL-2.0"
├── icon.png
├── preload.json            # 28 font entries + 2 custom atlases
├── modules/                # Lua libraries: modules/kompot.lua + modules/kompot/...
├── scripts/hud.lua         # HUD entry script — on_hud_open() (see 09)
├── layouts/                # gallery.xml + gallery.xml.lua (layout + companion script, see 09)
├── config/bindings.toml    # [kompot] gallery = "key:f12"
├── texts/                  # en_US.txt, ru_RU.txt — incl. dotted keys
├── fonts/                  # IBM Plex TTFs (out of scope)
├── textures/               # UI skin/icons textures (out of scope)
├── annotations/            # editor/LLM Lua annotations (out of scope)
├── docs/, art/, LICENSES/, CHANGELOG.md, README.md   # repo hygiene, engine ignores
```

Takeaways relevant to pack authors:

- `package.json` extra field `"license"` is tolerated (engine ignores unknown
  fields). Metadata for humans goes fine there.
- A pack CAN ship pure code/assets with zero blocks and zero items — Kompot has
  no `blocks/` or `items/` folder at all.
- `preload.json` fonts use object entries:
  `{"name": "kompot_12", "path": "fonts/IBMPlexSans-Regular.ttf", "size": 12}`
  — font NAMES are how other content references them.
- `config/bindings.toml` binds a pack action to a key:
  ```toml
  [kompot]
  gallery = "key:f12"
  ```
- Localization files mix content-caption style keys and dotted keys:
  `kompot.gallery=Kompot / Gallery`.
- Consuming packs declare `"dependencies": ["kompot"]` and call its modules via
  `require "kompot:kompot"` — modules are namespaced by pack id (Lua topic).

## Which files in these repos are engine-relevant vs ignored

Engine-relevant (affect loading/content): `package.json`, `icon.png`,
`preload.json`, `content.json` (generated), `blocks/`, `items/`,
`block_materials/`, `textures/`, `texts/`, `config/`, plus the out-of-scope
content folders listed in 02.

Ignored by the engine (repo hygiene, safe to keep for humans/LLMs): `README.md`,
`CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`, `LICENSES/`, `docs/`, `art/`, `annotations/`,
`*.toml` at project level. DO keep them — they cost nothing and help everyone.

## When to copy what

- Starting a new pack → copy the *shape* of `my_pack` (minimal + only needed folders).
- Need items with behavior → look at `my_pack/items/*` + its scripts, then read
  engine scripting docs before writing your own.
- Need the game-shell around packs → that is a project; out of scope, see stub.
- Need UI → Kompot's own docs (`docs/` inside fork_of_kompot) are the entry point.


<!-- ===== docs/08-pitfalls.md ===== -->

# 08. Pitfalls and Pre-flight Checklist

Every entry below is a real failure mode — either documented upstream, thrown
by the engine, or observed in real packs. Treat each AVOID as a hard rule.

## Fatal mistakes

1. **Editing `content.json`.** It is auto-generated and used to convert world
   saves. Manual edits corrupt worlds irreversibly (upstream warning).
   AVOID creating, editing, or deleting it in source repos.
2. **Missing `package.json`.** A folder without it is not a pack — the scanner
   skips it. DO always start from the manifest.
3. **Invalid pack ID.** Outside `a-z0-9_`, starting with a digit, or shorter
   than 2 / longer than 24 chars breaks registration. Reserved IDs (`res`,
   `user`, `world`, `project`, `config`, `core`) are unavailable. `[VERIFIED]`
4. **`texture-faces` with fewer than 6 entries.** The engine throws
   "texture-faces requires 6 elements" and the pack fails to load.
   `[OBSERVED: engine source]`
5. **Using `texture` and `texture-faces` together.** Documented as incompatible;
   pick one. `[DOC]`
6. **Paths or extensions in texture names.** `"texture": "blocks/dirt.png"` is
   wrong. The value is a NAME resolved inside an atlas: `"dirt"` or
   `"blocks:dirt"` depending on context. `[VERIFIED]`
7. **Using `base:*` properties without depending on `base`.** `base:durability`
   and `base:loot` are registered by the `base` pack; without
   `"dependencies": ["base"]` they are not guaranteed to exist. `[VERIFIED]`
8. **Loot referencing a block instead of its item.** `base:loot[].item` needs an
   ITEM id; a block's item is `<pack>:<block>.item`. `[VERIFIED]`

## Likely-wrong assumptions (seen in practice)

9. **Assuming folder name = pack ID.** The engine keys packs by the `"id"` in
   `package.json`; the folder name is free-form and has NO meaning to the
   engine. In real packs the folder name almost always DIFFERS from the ID
   (e.g. folder `kompot_0f9103ff-1.2.2` ships `"id": "kompot"`), and exact
   matches are rare. NEVER infer a pack's ID from its folder name — read the
   manifest. `[OBSERVED]`
10. **Assuming `icon.png` must be 128x128.** It is a recommendation; 64x64 and
    210x208 exist in working packs. Keep it square. `[OBSERVED]`
11. **Assuming texture sizes are enforced.** Stock uses 16x16; other sizes are
    uncharted. DO stay 16x16 for blocks/items.
12. **Assuming `version` matters for pack resolution.** When two sources carry
    the same pack ID, priority decides; version is ignored. `[DOC]`
13. **Assuming a pack needs content.** A folder containing ONLY `package.json`
    is a complete, valid, loadable pack — nothing else is required. Blocks,
    items, textures, config and code are all optional extras (Kompot ships no
    blocks/items; confirmed first-hand). `[VERIFIED]`
14. **Inventing dependency version operators.** Only `@>=x.y` and `*` are
    documented. AVOID `<`, `<=`, `=`, ranges. `[DOC]`
15. **Capitalizing captions yourself.** Docs recommend lowercase captions; the
    engine upper-cases for display. Localization keys must match the lowercase
    caption string. `[DOC]`
16. **Preloading auto-loaded assets.** Block/item atlas textures are picked up
    automatically; preloading them is noise (upstream warns to keep preload
    minimal). `[DOC]`
17. **Putting `pack_id:` into `<image src>` or `menu.page`.** These do NOT use
    the pack namespace: `src` without a colon is a global texture name; `src`
    with a colon is `atlas_name:tile_name`; `menu.page` takes a bare page name
    scanned across all packs. Pack-qualified ids belong only to layout ids
    (`hud.show_overlay("pack:layout")`) and document paths
    (`gui.load_document`). See 09-hud-and-ui.md. `[VERIFIED]`
18. **Spelling the animation folder or preload key `animations`.** The engine
    constant is `animation` (singular): pack folder `animation/`, `preload.json`
    key `"animation"`. An upstream quirk you must reproduce. `[VERIFIED]`

## JSON hygiene

- AVOID trailing commas and comments — block/item files are strict JSON.
- DO keep UTF-8 (localization values are non-ASCII routinely).
- DO keep one definition per file; the file name is the content name.

## Pre-flight checklist (run before delivering a pack)

Manifest:
- [ ] `package.json` exists, parses, has `id`/`title`/`version`.
- [ ] `id` passes rules and is not reserved. Folder name is free-form — it
      does NOT need to equal `id`.
- [ ] `dependencies` lists every pack whose `pack:` references you use.

Content:
- [ ] Every `blocks/*.json` and `items/*.json` uses only properties documented
      in 03/04 (or upstream docs) — nothing invented.
- [ ] `texture-faces` arrays have exactly 6 entries in west/east/bottom/top/
      north/south order.
- [ ] No `texture` + `texture-faces` in the same block.
- [ ] Every texture/icon name resolves to a real PNG in `textures/blocks/` or
      `textures/items/`.
- [ ] `base:*` properties used only with `base` dependency; loot items use
      `.item` suffix where needed.

Assets & config:
- [ ] `icon.png` present at pack root (square).
- [ ] `preload.json` (if present) contains only genuinely needed entries.
- [ ] `texts/*.txt` keys match captions exactly (lowercase, spaces not
      underscores).
- [ ] No `content.json` committed from your side.

UI (09):
- [ ] Layout XMLs sit at `layouts/*.xml` (flat folder); menu pages at
      `layouts/pages/`.
- [ ] No pack id in `menu.page` names or in `<image src>` values.
- [ ] Animation folder/key spelled `animation` (singular), if used.

Runtime:
- [ ] Pack loads without errors in the engine log/console.
- [ ] Blocks appear in the content/inventory screen and place correctly.
- [ ] Loot drops, lights emit, plants sit on ground — as designed.

## Debugging hints

- Load errors are printed by the engine with the failing pack and file name
  (e.g. unknown model, JSON parse errors, missing textures render as
  `notfound`). Read the console output first. `[OBSERVED]`
- A pack that loads but shows missing textures/`notfound` icons indicates a
  name/folder mismatch (03/05 rules), not a manifest problem.
- The in-game console and engine logging are documented in the engine repo
  (`doc/ru/console.md`, mirrored as `doc/en/console.md`) — out of scope here.


<!-- ===== docs/09-hud-and-ui.md ===== -->

# 09. HUD and UI Basics (layouts, pages, overlays)

This document covers the PACK-SIDE mechanics of shipping UI: where layout files
live, how the engine registers and addresses them, and the ways to put them on
screen. It intentionally does NOT duplicate the full XML element reference or
the Lua GUI API — pointers to the authoritative upstream docs are at the end.

Minimal Lua appears here because UI cannot be triggered without at least one
script. Everything else stays declarative.

## The one rule that prevents most mistakes

Blocks and items live in ONE namespaced registry (`pack_id:name`, see
01-engine-overview.md). UI does NOT use that registry uniformly — it mixes
THREE different addressing schemes (document ids, menu page names, texture
names; the document-id scheme comes in two flavors, see rows 1–2):

| What you write                            | Scheme                       | Example                  |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Layout document id (`hud.*`)              | `pack_id:file_stem`, derived by the engine | `kompot:gallery` |
| Document alias (`gui.load_document` arg 2, iframe `src`) | any alias YOU invent | `my_pack:extra_panel` |
| Menu page name (`menu.page`)              | bare name, NO pack id        | `settings`               |
| `<image src>` texture                     | global name OR `atlas:tile`  | `gui/error`, `blocks:dirt` |

DO memorize this table. The most common LLM errors are putting `pack_id:` into
`menu.page` or `<image src>`, or omitting it in `hud.show_overlay`. `[VERIFIED]`

## UI-relevant folder layout

```text
my_pack/
├── layouts/
│   ├── hello.xml              # auto-registered as document "my_pack:hello"
│   ├── hello.xml.lua          # optional companion script (same name + .lua)
│   ├── pages/                 # menu pages for pagebox (menu.page)
│   │   ├── greeting.xml
│   │   └── some_dir/          # subfolders ARE allowed inside pages/
│   │       └── extra.xml      #   -> menu.page = "some_dir/extra"
│   └── templates/             # templates for gui.template()
├── scripts/
│   └── hud.lua                # per-pack HUD entry script (on_hud_open)
└── config/
    └── bindings.toml          # key bindings (format in 02-pack-structure.md)
```

Registration rules (`[VERIFIED: engine source]`):

- Every TOP-LEVEL `layouts/*.xml` of every pack is auto-loaded as a UI document
  named `<pack_id>:<file_stem>`. `layouts/hello.xml` -> `my_pack:hello`.
- The scan is FLAT: `layouts/pages/` and `layouts/templates/` are NOT
  auto-registered this way (they are consumed by `menu.page` and
  `gui.template()` respectively).
- There is NO `layouts` key in `preload.json`. Layouts are always loaded
  automatically; the preload keys are exactly: `animation`, `atlases`, `fonts`,
  `models`, `post-effects`, `shaders`, `skeletons`, `sounds`, `textures`.
  `[VERIFIED]`
- A companion script named `<file>.xml.lua` (e.g. `hello.xml.lua`) becomes the
  layout's script environment; functions defined there are callable from the
  XML's `onclick` attributes. `[OBSERVED: engine layouts + kompot]`

## Way 1 — HUD overlays and windows (`hud.*`, pack id REQUIRED)

The `hud` Lua library opens pack layouts on top of the game. The layout id is
ALWAYS pack-qualified here: `"pack_id:stem"`. `[DOC + VERIFIED]`

Key functions (full list upstream, see pointers):

```lua
-- Show layout as an overlay. Shows player inventory too if playerinv=true.
-- args (optional table) is passed to the layout's on_open.
hud.show_overlay("my_pack:hello", playerinv, args)

-- Open a layout bound to an inventory (like a chest screen). Returns invid.
-- Throws an exception if the layout does not exist.
hud.open("my_pack:my_window", disable_player_inv, invid)

-- Add a layout to the screen permanently (removed on world close only).
hud.open_permanent("my_pack:status_bar")

hud.close("my_pack:hello")     -- remove layout
hud.is_open("my_pack:hello")   -- -> bool

-- Block UI: opens the ui-layout of the block at x,y,z plus its inventory.
hud.open_block(x, y, z)        -- -> invid, layoutid
```

`[DOC]` for signatures; the `pack_id:stem` id format is `[VERIFIED]` (engine
registers layouts under exactly that name).

### scripts/hud.lua — the HUD entry script

Each pack MAY ship one special script: `scripts/hud.lua`. The engine registers
it as `<pack_id>:scripts/hud.lua` (type `hud`) and calls its `on_hud_open()`
when the in-game HUD opens (world joined). DO register your input callbacks and
open permanent HUD elements there — not at file scope. `[VERIFIED]`

```lua
-- my_pack/scripts/hud.lua
function on_hud_open()
    -- runs every time the HUD (re)opens; safe place for input.add_callback
end
```

Upstream events doc lists `on_hud_open(playerid)`; real packs define it with no
parameters — both forms appear in the wild. `[OBSERVED]`

### Key binding -> callback wiring (complete chain)

A pack action bound to a key is THREE files that must agree:

1. `config/bindings.toml` — section = pack id, key = action name:
   ```toml
   [my_ui_pack]
   hello = "key:h"
   ```
2. `scripts/hud.lua` — callback name is the DOTTED form `pack_id.action`:
   ```lua
   function on_hud_open()
       input.add_callback("my_ui_pack.hello", function()
           -- your toggle logic
       end)
   end
   ```
3. `texts/*.txt` (optional) — display name for the binding, same dotted key:
   `my_ui_pack.hello=Toggle hello overlay`

`[OBSERVED: kompot ships exactly this chain: [kompot] gallery = "key:f12" ->
input.add_callback("kompot.gallery", ...) -> kompot.gallery=Kompot / Gallery]`

### Real-world example (kompot, simplified)

`fork_of_kompot` toggles its gallery overlay with F12 — the exact pattern to
copy: `scripts/hud.lua` registers the callback, then:

```lua
if hud.is_open("kompot:gallery") then
    hud.close("kompot:gallery")
else
    hud.show_overlay("kompot:gallery", false)
end
```

and `layouts/gallery.xml.lua` (the layout's own companion script) calls
`hud.close("kompot:gallery")` from its close button. `[OBSERVED]`

## Way 2 — Menu pages (`menu.page`, NO pack id)

The main menu is a `pagebox` element; the global `menu` object IS the root menu
pagebox. Setting `menu.page` swaps the displayed page. `[OBSERVED: engine
stdlib `menu = _GUI_ROOT.menu`; documented in upstream projects.md]`

```lua
menu.page = "settings"          -- open page "settings"
menu.page = "content?mode=world" -- page with query arguments
menu.page = ""                  -- close the current page
```

How the lookup works (`[VERIFIED: engine source gui_util.lua]`):

1. The engine takes the page name (everything before `?` in the query).
2. It searches `layouts/pages/<name>.xml` across the core and ALL loaded packs
   — a plain virtual-filesystem find. The page name carries NO pack id and
   there is NO syntax to specify one.
3. The FIRST match in the file-system search order wins; the found document is
   loaded as `<pack>:pages/<name>` and its `on_open` receives the parsed query
   arguments.
4. Subfolders work: `menu.page = "some_dir/extra"` loads
   `layouts/pages/some_dir/extra.xml`. `[VERIFIED: format string + user
   confirmation]`

Consequences you MUST respect:

- DO use distinctive page names for your pack's pages. A page named like an
  engine page (`main`, `settings`, `content`, `pause`, `worlds`, ...) will
  SHADOW the built-in one when your pack has search priority (user:content
  ranks above res:content). This override trick is how game projects replace
  the main menu — DO NOT trigger it accidentally. `[OBSERVED]`
- AVOID assuming your page loads "from your pack" — if another pack ships a
  page with the same name and higher priority, its page wins.
- Pages are NOT auto-loaded at startup; they load on demand when addressed.

Pages also get companion scripts: `layouts/pages/greeting.xml` +
`greeting.xml.lua`. Engine pages use `@Label` texts resolved through
localization; plain text strings also work. `[OBSERVED: engine layouts]`

## Way 3 — Direct document loading (advanced)

For custom shells (project main menus, embedded panels):

```lua
-- Load any layout as a document; path IS pack-qualified here. [DOC]
gui.load_document(
    "my_pack:layouts/extra/panel.xml",  -- arg 1: path to the xml (a REAL file on disk)
    "my_pack:extra_panel",              -- arg 2: an ALIAS you invent for the loaded document
    {}                                  -- arg 3: args -> on_open
)

-- Then embed it, e.g. via an iframe element added to the root:
gui.root.root:add(
    "<iframe id='panel_frame' src='my_pack:extra_panel' " ..
    "size-func='unpack(gui.get_viewport())'/>"
)
```

Arg 2 ("my_pack:extra_panel") is an ALIAS, not a path. The engine does not look
it up on disk and does not derive it from the xml file name — you may pick any
string, and it never has to match `panel.xml`. The alias exists purely as the
HANDLE to the loaded document: the iframe `src` above embeds the document by
this exact alias. DO keep aliases unique and pack-prefixed
(`my_pack:whatever`) so two packs cannot pick colliding labels — a convention
this guide recommends, not a verified engine rule. `[VERIFIED: alias semantics
confirmed by the user first-hand]`

`[OBSERVED: wooden_meat_game start.lua does exactly this with its menu pack:
gui.load_document("wooden_meat_menu:layouts/main_menu/main_menu.xml",
"wooden_meat_menu:main_menu") + iframe add]`

Note that wooden_meat's alias (`wooden_meat_menu:main_menu`) happens to equal
`pack_id:file_stem` of its xml — that is their naming choice, NOT an engine
requirement. DO NOT generalize from that example.

Related helpers (all `[DOC]`): `gui.template(name, params)` renders templates
from `layouts/templates/`; `gui.root` is the root document; `gui.show_message`,
`gui.ask`, `gui.alert`, `gui.confirm` show ready-made dialogs.

### Block UI (declarative, no code to open)

Blocks can carry their own screens: give the block `"inventory-size": N` and
optionally `"ui-layout": "pack:layout"` (default: the block's own id ->
`pack/layouts/<block_name>.xml`). Opening is engine-driven (`hud.open_block`,
right-click etc.). See 03-blocks.md for the block properties. `[DOC]`

## XML essentials (the 20% you need most)

Layouts are XML files with a single root element. Element types include:
`container`, `panel`, `button`, `label`, `image`, `textbox`, `checkbox`,
`trackbar`, `select`, `canvas`, `iframe`, `pagebox`, `inventory`, `slot`,
`slots-grid`, `splitbox`, `bindbox`. `[DOC]`

Most-used common attributes (`[DOC]`, full list upstream):

- `id` — element id; ids are global within the document and are how scripts
  reach the element (`document["my_button"]`).
- `pos`, `size`, `min-size` — 2D vectors as strings: `"500,200"`.
- `margin`, `padding` — 4D vectors: `"left,top,right,bottom"`.
- `color` — RGBA hex: `"#FF8000"`, `"#FFFFFF80"`.
- `visible`, `enabled`, `interactive`, `scrollable`, `z-index`.
- `gravity` — auto-positioning inside the container: `top-left` ...
  `center-center` ... `bottom-right`.
- `position-func`, `size-func` — Lua expressions evaluated on layout/resize
  (engine layouts use `unpack(gui.get_viewport())` for fullscreen roots).
- Event handlers: `onclick`, `onrightclick`, `ondoubleclick`, `onfocus`,
  `ondefocus`, `onmouseenter`, `onmouseleave`, ... — Lua expressions, usually
  calls into the companion script (`onclick='close_self()'`).

Script-side access (companion script or any script after load): the global
`document` table indexes elements by id — `document["my_label"].text = "hi"`,
`document["box"]:destruct()`. Properties per element type are listed upstream
(scripting/ui.md). `[DOC]`

Inventory warning (`[DOC]`): `<inventory>` position is engine-controlled
(`pos`/`margin` do not apply), and slots not linked to an inventory id are not
displayed (`inventory_ui.inventory = invid` links them).

## `<image src>` — texture addressing without pack ids

`<image>` resolves `src` through the ASSET system, not the pack namespace.
Resolution rules (`[VERIFIED: engine source, get_texture_region]`):

1. **No colon** in `src` -> looked up as a global TEXTURE asset name:
   `src="gui/error"` -> engine texture `gui/error` (preloaded from the
   engine's own `res/preload.json`). No pack id, no extension.
2. **With colon** -> treated as `atlas_name:tile_name` — an ATLAS lookup, NOT
   a pack id: `src="blocks:dirt"` (blocks atlas), `src="items:shotgun"`,
   `src="kompot_ui_icons:pen"` (custom atlas).
3. Missing texture -> `fallback` attribute is tried; otherwise the image
   renders empty.

How to show YOUR OWN PNG in XML UI — two options:

- Global texture: put the PNG under `textures/` (e.g.
  `textures/gfx/my_pic.png`) and list `"gfx/my_pic"` in `preload.json`'s
  `"textures"` array. Then `src="gfx/my_pic"`. The name is GLOBAL — DO prefix
  it with something pack-specific to avoid collisions (wooden_meat_game uses
  `gfx/muzzle_flash`; kompot prefixes everything `kompot_*`). `[VERIFIED]`
- Custom atlas: declare an atlas in `preload.json` (`"atlases":
  [{"name": "my_pack_ui"}]`), put PNGs into `textures/my_pack_ui/`, and use
  `src="my_pack_ui:<file_stem>"`. `[OBSERVED: kompot does this for its UI
  skin/icons]`

Engine GUI textures live under the reserved-looking `gui/` name — DO NOT name
your textures `gui/...`; the engine ones would collide or confuse.

## Minimal working example (complete pack)

A pack that adds a toggleable overlay on key H. Four files, all complete and
final. Pack name: `my_ui_pack`.

```text
my_ui_pack/
├── package.json
├── config/bindings.toml
├── layouts/hello.xml
├── layouts/hello.xml.lua
└── scripts/hud.lua
```

`package.json`:

```json
{
    "id": "my_ui_pack",
    "title": "My UI Pack",
    "version": "0.1.0",
    "description": "Toggleable hello overlay"
}
```

No `dependencies` needed: `hud`, `input`, `gui` are engine built-ins, and no
`base:*` properties are referenced.

`config/bindings.toml`:

```toml
[my_ui_pack]
hello = "key:h"
```

`layouts/hello.xml`:

```xml
<container
    id="root"
    color="#00000080"
    position-func="0,0"
    size-func="unpack(gui.get_viewport())"
>
    <panel size="320,140" padding="16" interval="8"
           gravity="center-center" color="#507090E0">
        <label text="Hello from my_ui_pack" gravity="top-center"/>
        <button onclick='close_self()'>Close</button>
    </panel>
</container>
```

`layouts/hello.xml.lua`:

```lua
function on_open(args)
    -- args comes from hud.show_overlay(..., args) / gui.load_document(..., args)
    print("hello overlay opened")
end

function close_self()
    hud.close("my_ui_pack:hello")
end
```

`scripts/hud.lua`:

```lua
function on_hud_open()
    input.add_callback("my_ui_pack.hello", function()
        if hud.is_open("my_ui_pack:hello") then
            hud.close("my_ui_pack:hello")
        else
            hud.show_overlay("my_ui_pack:hello", false)
        end
    end)
end
```

Verify: enable the pack for a world, join it, press H — the overlay toggles;
Close and H both dismiss it; the engine log shows no errors.

## DO / AVOID summary

- DO use `hud.show_overlay("pack_id:stem", ...)` with the pack id — it is
  REQUIRED there.
- DO use bare names for `menu.page` — pack ids are IMPOSSIBLE there.
- DO use global texture names or `atlas:tile` in `<image src>` — never
  `pack_id:...`.
- DO treat the `gui.load_document` document id as a free-form ALIAS you invent
  (not a path) — and keep it pack-prefixed and unique (see Way 3).
- DO register input callbacks inside `scripts/hud.lua`'s `on_hud_open()`.
- DO give custom global texture/font/asset names a pack-specific prefix.
- DO copy the engine's own `res/layouts/` as format examples — they are
  authoritative and always up to date.
- AVOID naming your pages `main`, `settings`, `content`, `pause`, `worlds` —
  you will shadow built-in menu pages (or get shadowed).
- AVOID subfolders directly under `layouts/` expecting auto-registration —
  only top-level `layouts/*.xml` auto-registers (`pages/` and `templates/`
  are special).
- AVOID preloading layouts in `preload.json` — there is no such key.
- AVOID the spelling `animations` for the folder or preload key — the engine
  constant is `animation` (singular). `[VERIFIED]`

## UI-specific pitfalls

1. **Putting `pack_id:` into `menu.page` or `<image src>`.** See the addressing
   table at the top; these schemes do not use pack ids. `[VERIFIED]`
2. **Omitting the pack id in `hud.*` calls.** `hud.show_overlay("hello", ...)`
   will not find `my_pack:hello` and throws. `[DOC]`
3. **Nesting layouts deeper than one level.** `layouts/sub/x.xml` is NOT
   auto-registered; only `layouts/*.xml` is. Pages must be under
   `layouts/pages/`. `[VERIFIED]`
4. **Expecting `layouts/pages/` files at startup.** Pages load on demand only.
   `[VERIFIED]`
5. **Binding mismatch across the 3-file chain.** `bindings.toml` action
   `hello` in section `[my_ui_pack]` must match callback name
   `"my_ui_pack.hello"` exactly. `[OBSERVED]`
6. **Editing a page while it is open and expecting hot reload.** UI changes
   need a world/menu reload; DO restart to verify.
7. **Treating the `gui.load_document` document id as a path.** It is an ALIAS
   you invent (Way 3): not read from disk, not derived from the file name, no
   match with the xml required. `[VERIFIED: user first-hand]`

## Upstream pointers (read before writing real UI)

The paths below are files of the ENGINE's own repository
(github.com/MihailRis/voxelcore, folder `doc/`) — NOT files of this guide.
Each topic exists twice: `doc/en/` (English) and `doc/ru/` (Russian). The
Russian documentation is usually MORE complete and more current; when the two
diverge, prefer `doc/ru/`. File names match on both sides:

| Topic                                        | English (`doc/en/`)                    | Russian (`doc/ru/`) — prefer this |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| FULL XML element and attribute reference     | `doc/en/xml-ui-layouts.md`             | `doc/ru/xml-ui-layouts.md`             |
| Element properties/methods from Lua          | `doc/en/scripting/ui.md`               | `doc/ru/scripting/ui.md`               |
| `gui.*` API (dialogs, documents, templates)  | `doc/en/scripting/builtins/libgui.md`  | `doc/ru/scripting/builtins/libgui.md`  |
| `hud.*` API                                  | `doc/en/scripting/builtins/libhud.md`  | `doc/ru/scripting/builtins/libhud.md`  |
| Input callbacks and key codes                | `doc/en/scripting/builtins/libinput.md`| `doc/ru/scripting/builtins/libinput.md`|
| `on_hud_open` and other events               | `doc/en/scripting/events.md`           | `doc/ru/scripting/events.md`           |
| `menu.page`, main-menu replacement           | `doc/en/projects.md`                   | `doc/ru/projects.md`                   |

Also in the engine repository:

- `res/layouts/` — the engine's own layouts (pages, templates, console,
  inventory); authoritative and always up-to-date format examples.
- Real packs: `fork_of_kompot` (`layouts/gallery.xml*`, `scripts/hud.lua`),
  `wooden_meat_game` (`start.lua` document embedding, `wooden_meat_menu`
  pack).

Lua scripting beyond these UI entry points is out of scope of this guide (see
README scope table and docs/stubs/).

  `model-name` without `<pack>:models/` prefix or extension `[DOC]`; model

# STUB — Projects & World Generators (NOT COVERED YET)

Status: **intentionally out of scope of this guide. TODO: write full documents.**

Two related-but-separate topics were excluded:

## Projects (`project.toml`)
What belongs here: project manifests (`name`, `title`, `base_packs`,
`permissions`), running with `--project <path>`, project-level scripts
(`start.lua`, `project_client.lua`), `project:content` source.

Known facts already documented in-scope: `project.toml` with `base_packs =
["base", ...]` enables default packs `[OBSERVED]`; `project:content` has
priority above `res:content` `[DOC]`.

Authoritative sources: `<voxelcore repo>/doc/ru/projects.md` and real example
<https://github.com/George-Noise/wooden_meat_game> (root `project.toml`).

## World generators (`generators/`)
What belongs here: generator TOML + scripting (`demo.toml`, `demo.files` in the
stock pack), biome/ore/height configuration.

Authoritative sources: `<voxelcore repo>/doc/ru/world-generator.md` (RU only —
the largest engine doc, absent from EN set).

Until these stubs are replaced:

- DO NOT guess project flags or generator TOML fields.
- A typical ADD-ON content pack needs neither — a pack is usable from the
  content menu of any world.
